changelog: agat_statistics: one panel per metric with its own axis, instead of one bar per annotation summing unlike metrics; a Metric selector.
agat_gene_models: titles and descriptions on every render; log genes axis, median line and labelled points on genes_vs_exons.

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: genes_vs_exons
  title: Genes against exons per transcript
  description: |-
    Each point is an annotation and a transcript type, with the number of genes on the horizontal axis (log scale) and the exons per transcript on the vertical axis, sized by mean gene length and coloured by transcript type. It answers how complete the gene models of each annotation look.
    How to read: a fragmented annotation shows many short, few-exon models, so it sits low on the vertical axis. Points of one transcript type that sit apart from the others are the annotation to inspect first. AGAT publishes no cut-off for these values.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median exons per transcript of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of AGAT.
    Source: https://agat.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tools/agat_sp_statistics.html
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Genes
    y_title: Exons per transcript
    log_x: true
    top_n_labels: 6
    legend_pos: bottom
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: genes
    y: exons_per_transcript
    label: genome
    color: feature_type
    size: mean_gene_length

- component: figure
  title: Genes per annotation by type
  description: |-
    Each bar is an annotation, with its genes stacked by transcript type such as mRNA, lncRNA or tRNA. It answers how many genes each annotation holds and of what kind.
    How to read: compare annotations of related species, whose gene counts should be of the same order. A bar with almost no non-coding types may reflect an annotation that only kept protein-coding genes.
    Source: https://agat.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tools/agat_sp_statistics.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: genome
    y: genes
    color: feature_type
    barmode: stack
    labels:
      genome: Annotation
      genes: Genes
      feature_type: Transcript type

- component: card
  id: gene_count
  title: Protein-coding genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of mRNA genes over the annotations, and the bar splits them by annotation, with the median and maximum annotation beside it. It answers how many protein-coding genes the annotations hold.
    How to read: a thin share is an annotation with far fewer genes than the others, which may be incomplete.
    Source: https://agat.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tools/agat_sp_statistics.html
  column: genes
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: genome
  filter_expr: col('feature_type') == 'mrna'
  caption: protein-coding genes, by annotation

- component: card
  id: exons_per_transcript
  title: Exons per transcript
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of exons per mRNA, and the box shows the spread between annotations. It answers how rich the gene structures are.
    How to read: a lower value than related annotations suggests fragmented gene models that lack exons. The report counts the longest isoform of each gene for the per-transcript shape.
    Source: https://agat.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tools/agat_sp_statistics.html
  column: exons_per_transcript
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('feature_type') == 'mrna'
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: single_exon_share
  title: Single-exon genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent of mRNA genes made of one exon, and the box shows the spread between annotations. It answers how many gene models are a single exon.
    How to read: an annotation with a share far above its peers holds many short, possibly fragmented, models. Check it against the exons per transcript tile.
    Source: https://agat.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tools/agat_sp_statistics.html
  column: single_exon_gene_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('feature_type') == 'mrna'
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Gene models per annotation
  description: |-
    Each row is an annotation and a transcript type, with its genes, transcripts, exons, single-exon genes, overlapping genes and the mean lengths of genes, transcripts, exons, introns and CDS. It answers the exact numbers behind every other tile.
    How to read: filter by transcript type to compare annotations on one kind of model.

- component: figure
  version: 1.1.0
  title: AGAT metrics per annotation
  description: |-
    Each panel is one sp_statistics metric, and each bar in it the value for one annotation in the longest-isoform view, which keeps one transcript per gene. It answers how annotations compare metric by metric.
    How to read: every panel has its own value axis, so compare bars within a panel, not across panels. Without a metric filter the first nine metrics in AGAT's order are shown; pick metrics and a feature type with the filters to see others.
    Lines and annotations: no reference line is drawn, because each panel holds a different quantity and a cohort median of a handful of annotations says little.
    Source: https://agat.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tools/agat_sp_statistics.html
  code: |-
    # one isoform view, so a bar is one number: the longest-isoform view when present
    view = "longest" if (df["isoforms"] == "longest").any() else "all"
    d = df.filter(pl.col("isoforms") == view).drop_nulls(["value"])
    # the first metrics in AGAT's order, unless the metric filter picked others
    keep = d.sort("metric_order")["metric"].unique(maintain_order=True).head(9).to_list()
    d = d.filter(pl.col("metric").is_in(keep)).sort(["metric_order", "genome"])
    fig = px.bar(
        d.to_pandas(),
        x="genome",
        y="value",
        color="genome",
        facet_col="metric",
        facet_col_wrap=3,
        facet_row_spacing=0.12,
        category_orders={"metric": keep},
        labels={"genome": "Annotation", "value": "Value", "metric": "Metric"},
    )
    fig.for_each_annotation(lambda a: a.update(text=a.text.split("=", 1)[-1]))
    fig.update_yaxes(matches=None, showticklabels=True, title_text="")
    fig.update_xaxes(showticklabels=False, title_text="")
    fig.update_layout(
        legend_title_text=f"Annotation ({view} isoforms)",
        margin={"t": 32, "l": 48, "r": 16, "b": 24},
    )

- component: interactive
  title: Feature type
  description: Filters the dashboard to the feature types picked here, such as mRNA or lncRNA. It answers
    how one kind of feature compares between annotations.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: feature_type

- component: interactive
  version: 1.1.0
  title: Metric
  description: Picks one sp_statistics metric so that the chart shows a single panel and compares that quantity
    between annotations. It answers how annotations differ on that metric.
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: metric

- component: table
  title: Annotation statistics
  description: |-
    Each row is one number of the AGAT sp_statistics report, for an annotation, a feature type and an isoform view, in the order AGAT prints them. It answers the exact value behind the bar chart.
    How to read: filter by metric to compare one quantity, or by isoform view to separate all isoforms from the longest one.
    Source: https://agat.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tools/agat_sp_statistics.html
